bibliographic.title: Leveraging Foundation Models in Maternal and Child Health: A Systematic Review
bibliographic.authors: Xinnie Mai, Yunqian Liu, Philip Chung, Jonathan D. Reiss, Shuang Zhou, Ronald J. Wong, Mingquan Lin, Ivana Maric, Marina Sirota, Nima Aghaeepour, Rui Zhang, David K. Stevenson, Feng Xie
bibliographic.citation_apa: Mai, X., Liu, Y., Chung, P., Reiss, J. D., Zhou, S., Wong, R. J., Lin, M., Maric, I., Sirota, M., Aghaeepour, N., Zhang, R., Stevenson, D. K., & Xie, F. (2025). Leveraging foundation models in maternal and child health: A systematic review. medRxiv. https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.08.29.25333768

methodology.study_design: systematic literature review with PRISMA flow diagram
methodology.sample_description: Studies leveraging foundation models in maternal and child health published between 2020 and 2025; 785 studies screened, 63 met inclusion criteria
methodology.technology_context: Foundation models including GPT, BERT, ViT, LLaMA, and ChatGPT applied to maternal, neonatal, and pediatric clinical tasks such as diagnosis, documentation, and medical response generation

eligibility.exclusion_reason: Systematic review focused on clinical applications of foundation models in maternal and child health, not on conversational governance, oversight, accountability, or operational governance of conversational LLM systems in regulated settings.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the article is a systematic review covering foundation models and LLMs (including ChatGPT) in regulated healthcare (MCH), the stated objective and reported scope center on clinical task performance, multimodal integration, diagnostics, and documentation. The provided text contains no substantive treatment of conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, observability, audit, human oversight, contestation, compliance controls, or post-deployment monitoring of conversational AI systems. Term overlap from automated triage (e.g., ChatGPT, dialogue) reflects incidental mentions within included primary studies, not the review's governing focus.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Scope mismatch is clear from title, abstract, and study objectives; no ambiguous governance content requiring adjudication.

appraisal.notes: Appraised as a healthcare FM systematic review based on available front matter and abstract. Full methods, quality appraisal of included studies, and detailed synthesis were not provided in the excerpt. Not appraised for relevance to conversational governance because the study is out of scope for inclusion.

cerqual.explanation: Within its own domain (FM applications in MCH), the review appears methodologically coherent with PRISMA and a defined search window, but the excerpt provides limited detail on search strategy, risk-of-bias assessment, and synthesis methods. Relevance to the target review on conversational governance in regulated LLM systems is very low because governance, oversight, and conversational-system controls are not addressed.

coding.theme: Clinical application of foundation models in maternal and child health
coding.subtheme: Diagnostics, documentation, and medical content generation

synthesis.main_claim: Foundation models show strong potential to generalize across maternal and child health clinical tasks by integrating multimodal data for diagnosis, documentation, and medical response generation, but rigorous validation and clinician collaboration are needed for safe deployment.
synthesis.contribution: Maps 63 included studies (2020–2025) on foundation models in MCH and summarizes application areas across text, EHR, imaging, and temporal data.
synthesis.limitations: Provided excerpt does not detail full search strategy, quality appraisal, or governance-related gaps; preprint not peer reviewed.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central evidence on conversational governance; may serve only as peripheral bibliographic context for healthcare FM reviews unrelated to governance mechanisms.

evidence.claim: Study is a systematic review of foundation models in maternal and child health, not conversational governance.
evidence.excerpt: We conducted a systematic review to identify recent studies leveraging FMs in MCH published between 2020 and 2025.

evidence.claim: Regulated healthcare domain (maternal and child health).
evidence.excerpt: Maternal and child health (MCH) represents a critical domain requiring accurate, timely, and data-driven decision-making

evidence.claim: Sample size and screening process are reported.
evidence.excerpt: Of 785 studies, 63 met the inclusion criteria.

evidence.claim: Includes LLMs/ChatGPT among foundation models but for clinical tasks, not governance.
evidence.excerpt: Representative FM architectures include Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT)28, Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT)29,30, Vision Transformer (ViT)31,32 and Large Language Model Meta AI (LLaMA)33,34.
